summary: Nicholas Justin Allen worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Oxford, including under doctoral supervisor Rodney Needham, and at SOAS. He lectured at Durham (1972–1976) and Oxford (from 1976), later serving as Reader at Wolfson College.

Nicholas Roerich worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and the Imperial Academy of Arts. He served as director of the Imperial Society for the Encouragement of the Arts and president of Mir iskusstva.
Nicholas Witkowski specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at Stanford University by 2015 and was a research fellow at the University of Tokyo in 2017.
Nicholson T. Collier is a scholar in religious studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Paul J. Griffiths.

Nicola Di Cosmo works in Iranian/Central Asian studies, Sinology, and history. After earning his PhD from Indiana University (~1985–1991), he held posts at Harvard, Columbia, the University of Canterbury, and the Institute for Advanced Study.

Nicolaas Johannes Krom worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served at the Archaeological Service in the Netherlands East Indies (1913–1916) and held academic posts at Leiden University in 1919 and from 1925 to 1945.
Nicolaas van Wijk was a linguist who studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1898–1903) and Moscow State University (~1903–1904). He held a post at Leiden University starting in 1913.
Nicolas Morrissey specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Gregory Schopen and holds a post at the University of Georgia.

Nicolas Revire works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Silpakorn University, under doctoral supervisors Claudine Bautze-Picron and Peter Skilling, and held a post at Thammasat University (attested 2016).

Nicolas Tournadre works in linguistics and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at Sorbonne Nouvelle under Claude Hagège and held positions at INALCO, Paris 8, the University of Provence, and Aix-Marseille University.
Nicole Baden is active in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under traditional teacher Richard Baker and succeeded him in 2024.

Nicole Vandier-Nicolas worked in Sinology and history/archaeology. She taught at the École du Louvre (~1966) and served as professor of Chinese civilization at INALCO/École des langues orientales from ~1966 to 1977.

Niels Ludvig Westergaard worked in Indology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Copenhagen, Bonn (under Christian Lassen), Paris, London, and Oxford, later serving as professor and Rektor at the University of Copenhagen.

Nigel Allan is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Curator of Oriental Books and Manuscripts at the Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine, succeeding Marianne Winder (attested 1993).

Niharranjan Ray worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Calcutta, UCL, and Leiden, and held positions as professor at the University of Calcutta and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study.
Nika Jovic is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her Magistra der Philosophie at the University of Vienna, where she studied under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and Géza Bethlenfalvy.
Nikita Yakovlevich Bichurin worked in Sinology and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at the Kazan Theological Academy and held a post at the Département asiatique around 1826.

Nikolai Solmsdorf specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Munich under doctoral supervisor Franz-Karl Ehrhard and held a post at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2013).

Nile Green is a scholar of history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Manchester (~2005–2007) and the University of California, Los Angeles (~2008).

Nina Mirnig works in Indology and religious studies. She earned her DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson by 2010 and held a post at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2020).
